title: Quantitative lower bounds for trace reconstruction
summary: Exact worst-case reconstruction of a binary word from independent deletion traces requires $`n^{\Omega(\log\log n)}`$ samples for every fixed deletion probability $`q\in(0,1)`$, even with unrestricted computation and any fixed positive success probability. This gives a negative answer to the polynomial-sample question for binary trace reconstruction. More generally, when $`q^3\log n\to\infty`$, we prove a lower bound of $`n^{c\log(q^3\log n)}`$ samples for every fixed $`0\lt c\lt 1/(4\log2)`$. Here q is the known deletion probability, and all logarithms are natural.
family_title: Quantitative trace-reconstruction bounds with a uniform decoder

review.reason: Proves superpolynomial sample lower bounds for binary trace reconstruction from deletion traces.
